_comment: Venue coordinates the app pins directly, so it never has to search for a
Japanese venue name on the device. It cannot do that dependably: the map
service follows the device's region, and a China-region device searches a
map of mainland China alone. It answers most of these names with nothing,
and answers the rest by matching the kanji against Chinese places.
Curated rather than geocoded at run time. STU48 plays a small, repeating
set of venues, a wrong pin is worse than no pin, and a table is something
a person can check. Every entry records the address it came from and how
the coordinate was derived; keep doing that when adding one.
A venue that is not here simply publishes without a coordinate, and the
app falls back to searching by name — which still works in Japan. Run
`python scripts/venues.py --unlisted` to see what the live schedule is
using that this file does not cover.
WGS84, as the app and Apple Maps expect. Do not convert to GCJ-02: that
offset applies to data inside China and would move these off their venue.
Names are matched loosely — width, case, a 都道府県 prefix and a
parenthetical alias are all normalised away — so one spelling usually
covers the variants the official pages use. See scripts/venues.py.
